changes.current_line: Online and in-store on one platform; the line between them has pretty much disappeared.
changes.change: For retail buyers with stores, say: One system for your tills and your website: one customer, one basket. Back it with a live, step-by-step demo of an online order being returned at a store till, with the same customer record carrying through to loyalty. If we can't show the till return, don't lead with this line. Say "the tills", not "in-person payments" or "point of sale".
changes.why: Store ops dismissed our M3 line as "that's a diagram" and asked to watch a return at the till, which we only described, while the customer framed the problem in their own words ("One system for the tills and the website.", "one customer, one basket.") around the returns and split-record failure that started the deal.

changes.change: For COO and store-operations buyers, add a rollout and accountability proof point: One team accountable for your stores, end to end: a rollout plan with dates, who installs, what happens to the old tills, and who shows up when a till goes down. If a partner does the installs, name the single point of contact and state that we stay accountable, so the buyer is never left with "two vendors pointing at each other".
changes.why: The decider said "I don't want two vendors pointing at each other.", and our answer to who does the installs was a partner; we also never produced the rollout plan they asked for, while Adyen brought people who had done store rollouts and most of the customer's questions were about stores.

changes.current_line: Trusted by leading businesses; see our customer stories.
changes.change: For retail buyers, replace the case-study link with an offer to talk to a peer: Talk to a retailer running their tills and website with us. Use this only when a reference retailer is confirmed and available to take the call quickly, so we can set it up when asked.
changes.why: The decider asked "can I talk to them?" and we couldn't set up a call in time, while Adyen named retailers she knew, so pointing to customer stories was not the proof she wanted.
